newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Q3 newspaper advertising revenue up - group.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Q3 newspaper advertising revenue up - group.

text.p: U.S. newspaper classified advertising revenue was up 10.6 percent in the third quarter of 1996, the Newspaper Association of America said Tuesday.
Retail advertising grew by 3.3 percent and national advertising rose 18 percent, the association said.
Total advertising expenditures in newspapers for the first three quarters of 1996 grew by 6.2 percent over the same period in 1995, NAA said.
"The continued steady growth in advertising revenue reflects the healthy nature of newspapers across the country," NAA president John Sturm said.
In the third quarter, classifieds contributed $3.8 bln, retail accounted for $4.4 bln and national brought in $1.1 bln for a total of $9.3 bln, NAA said.
In the first nine months, total advertising revenue grew to $27 bln, from $25 bln for the first three quarters of 1995.
"The double-digit growth in classified advertising, which was supported by the continued growth in employment ads, signals the ongoing strength of the nation's economy overall," Sturm said.
